evidence: The paper develops methods for flexible calibration curves in clustered clinical prediction data. Its focus is on assessing agreement between predicted and observed event risks in multicenter validation studies (stated: "A comprehensive evaluation includes an assessment of the agreement between the estimated risks and the observed outcomes, also known as calibration"). Random forests appear once only, as a data-generating mechanism in synthetic data experiments to test calibration methods under nonlinear truth. No impurity-based importance (Gini, MDI, variance) is used, computed, or discussed. The paper contains no feature importance rankings, feature selection by importance, or magnitude interpretation of importance values.
